name: tool-agent-registry
context: Agent systems where multiple tools or subagents must be discovered, selected, and invoked dynamically at runtime. A registry maintains a queryable catalogue of available capabilities — with metadata on cost, latency, and quality — so the agent can programmatically pick the right tool or subagent for a task rather than relying on hardcoded tool lists.
benefits: Enables runtime tool discovery without redeploying the agent
Metadata (cost, latency, reliability) allows agents to make informed trade-offs
Supports dynamic registration of new tools or agents without restarting the system
Decouples tool producers from tool consumers — tools can evolve independently
tradeoffs: Registry must be kept in sync with actual tool availability
Adding a registry layer introduces latency on first tool selection
Registry metadata can become stale — tools may degrade without updating their entries
Increased system complexity for what a static tool list achieves simply
use_cases: Dynamic routing: an agent queries the registry for tools matching a task description
Multi-agent systems: workers discover available subagents and their capabilities at runtime
Tool versioning: new tool versions are registered alongside old ones; agents pick versions they trust
Cost-aware selection: agents filter tools by budget constraints stored in registry metadata
avoid_when: The toolset is fixed and known at design time
Latency requirements are so tight that registry lookup adds unacceptable overhead
All tools are guaranteed to be available and the agent has no choice to make
technology_stack: Vector similarity search over tool descriptions
anti_patterns: Registry that is never updated — metadata diverges from actual tool behavior
Agents that always pick the cheapest or fastest tool regardless of task fit
No fallback when the registry is unavailable — the agent cannot proceed
design_principles: Tool entries must include freshness metadata (last_updated) to detect stale entries
The registry must be durable and available at the same reliability level as the agent
Tool selection must have a defined fallback when the preferred tool is unavailable
best_practices: Include capability, cost, latency, and reliability metadata per tool entry
Version tool entries so agents can pin to known-good versions
Periodically health-check registered tools and mark degraded entries
references: Agent Patterns Catalog, Tool-Agent Registry pattern — https://www.agentpatternscatalog.org/patterns/tool-agent-registry/
